findings.fact: A complete constructed PMR read does not survive as selected row Project/FileMobId when cancellation happens before the physical header request. The physical row and complete PMR source receipt survive.
findings.nature: Runtime control-record result; not a genuine PMR pathology.

findings.fact: A complete genuine MXF header read loses FileMobId, ClipName, Project and physical duration when cancelled at finalising before row matching; the physical row and complete source receipt survive. Production MediaScanner reproduces this.
findings.nature: Runtime result using a disposable copy of genuine fixture bytes.

findings.fact: Cancel invoked synchronously from the final Scan complete log batch, after formatting but before scanFinished delivery, is not reflected in the captured session or Console: values remain and scan is reported complete.
findings.nature: Runtime late-publication boundary result through an existing production signal. Not a mid-adapter-loop timing reproduction.

compactReceiptReadiness.status: Audit only. Existing production safeguards passed; no compact receipt/storage implementation exists or was verified by this work.

equivalentsRequired.reason: Current evidence history identifies which header receipt/changed-source issue belongs to the transferred row; another row at a reused destination must not lend its receipt. Replace this dependency explicitly.

equivalentsRequired.data: Deliberately skipped header versus attempted/unreadable header; selected usable database FileMobId expectation when deliberately skipped.
equivalentsRequired.reason: Skipped-header Copy/Move/Delete must confirm the selected database identity through the subsequently opened header. Preserve the existing different policy for an attempted unreadable header.

equivalentsRequired.data: Header-established identity/corroboration and explicit unavailable changed/conflicting-header state, kept distinct from selected database-only master associations.
equivalentsRequired.reason: Database-only associations must not be imposed on the header, and a detected changed/conflicting header must not become an innocuous unknown identity after evidence removal. Exact compact encoding remains implementation work.

removalDependencies: Migrate opscanreceipt evidence/source traversal before deleting row MediaEvidence or shared complete ScanResult ownership.
Replace transfer-time filesystem/membership observations and original-owner lookup with compact row/receipt updates.

Preserve journal serialization and old-journal parsing compatibility. Current tests include several-master legacy scan claims; newly scanned Copland rows use one selected MasterMobId, without weakening separate header corroboration or rewriting old recovery claims.
Preserve source-changed exclusion and bounded changed-database header fallback; do not promote a read into completed usable metadata until necessary existing validation/selection is finished.
compactReceiptReadiness.selectedRisk: Current tests validate the old data shape. They are migration safeguards, not evidence that deleting fields or replacing receipts is already correct.

limits: No application/test source edits; only this owned durable evidence JSON was added to the repository. Temporary probes, fixtures, logs, objects and binaries remain outside it.
No file operation on original media/fixtures: operations suite compile-time fixture root points to disposable byte-for-byte copies. Original and copied seed bytes remain unchanged.
One case-distinct-name test skipped on the case-insensitive temporary filesystem. This does not verify that branch on a case-sensitive filesystem.
No real NEXIS/Windows workload, large scan, GUI manipulation, memory benchmark, future compact implementation or runtime memory ceiling verification.

Late cancellation is exercised after row formatting at final logging before result delivery. Mid-formatting cancellation remains a source-audited gap, not a separately reproduced runtime timing window.
These are current implementation results at the recorded source/build state; no future cancellation or retention improvement is claimed.
